messages:
maria: Heads-up — getting a handful of mobile reconnect loops after a TLS rekey on eu-west. clients show WS PONG delays then proxy force-closes, console shows idle -> resume billing spike :confused:
kevin: saw that too, eu1 proxy logs show STALLED_PONG > 30s then FIN. mobile carriers may hold sockets during rekey?
oliver: can you paste the proxy snippet?
maria: log excerpt:
```
[2025-03-22T14:02:11Z] conn=abcd123 state=WS_OPEN last_pong=2025-03-22T14:01:30Z
[2025-03-22T14:02:42Z] conn=abcd123 event=stalled_pong threshold=30s action=force_close code=1006
[2025-03-22T14:02:43Z] conn=abcd123 route=eu-west shard=3 resume_token=rt:xyz
```
kevin: thx. interesting part: resume_token present and client resumes quickly which triggers token billing path. console shows an idle flag then a resume line item. product-anna: users complain about charges and flicker in chat UI. we need clearer UX on console.
devex: agree — console should separate "inferred client hold" vs "server-initiated pause". right now both map to idle and then resume billing.
maria: proposal: add a small annotation we can infer when network rekey/OS background pause happened (heuristic: long unacked pings + immediate resume token reuse). label it "likely client hold (mobile/oncarrier)"
oliver: also API debate: should resume token be sent as a header on the WS upgrade or only in the first resume frame? current behavior sends resume token in a query param on reconnect which drives sticky routing. if we move it to an initial header it might be stripped by some proxies.
kevin: FYI some carrier proxies rewrite query params for caching reasons, headers are safer for privacy but may be dropped by old proxies. either way sticky routing is what prevents duplicate work but also creates billing race if resumed across two routes.
sre-bot: ALERT: spike detected: ws-resume-count eu-west shard3 14:02 -> +72 resumes in 2m. correlate with tls-rekey events.
product-anna: short-term: console change + billing note should reduce support tickets. long-term: routing change to prefer resume-token routing only after token verification?
devex: API suggestion for engineering debate: include resume token in a signed, short-lived header `x-rd-resume` (HMAC'd by control plane). control plane verifies and returns a sticky route cookie. advantage: prevents accidental duplicate resume across regions and lets us reject stale tokens (no double-bill). disadvantage: requires control-plane handshake on reconnect, adds latency on hot reconnects.
maria: sounds reasonable. add privacy check: header must be over TLS and tokens scoped to account id. also fallback to non-sticky mode if control plane unreachable.
oliver: implementation notes: we'd need a tiny handshake endpoint (/v1/ws-auth) that accepts token and returns route cookie. clients do an ephemeral HTTP POST before WS upgrade. mobile SDKs can batch this with reconnect backoff.
kevin: alternatively we can keep current query param resume but enhance proxy idempotency: when a route sees a resume token, it should check kvcache for active session and refuse duplicate accept if another route already accepted — i.e., central acceptance registry. that's more infra work but keeps client simple.
product-anna: which path is lower-risk for a Q2 patch?
maria: console annotation + billing label (quick) + short-term patch to reject duplicate resume acceptance (medium). control-plane header + handshake (larger).
devex: for console annotation we'll need new telemetry: add event `resume_inference_reason` with values ["client_hold_heuristic","network_drop","server_close","explicit_user_pause"]. that fits existing dashboards.
console-bot: NOTE: created alerting dashboard draft under /dashboards/streaming/reconnect-rootcause — linked to current incident.
kevin: ok i'll open infra PR for central acceptance registry prototype. maria please file a devex ticket for console annotation and product-anna can add billing note copy.
maria: filed: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DEVEX-1123 (console annotation + billing message).
kevin: opened infra task: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-9876 (central accept registry prototype).
product-anna: thanks — will prep support blurb and tweak dashboard wording.
maria: once prototype in place we'll run a canary in eu-west only. monitor resumes vs unique session IDs.
kevin: agreed. for immediate mitigation, bump the pong threshold to 45s for mobile clients behind carriers (config flag per-route). low-risk and should reduce forced-close churn.
oliver: +1. any objections?
product-anna: no objections. communicate to support.
maria: merging patch to per-route pong threshold now, will roll 10% canary in 5m.
sre-bot: DEPLOY: pong-threshold-route-config rolled to canary (eu-west shard3) at 2025-03-22T14:06:00Z by kevin.
